findings.claim: Bracketed IPv6 entries in NO_PROXY fail to exclude non-loopback IPv6 hosts, so the request can be sent through the proxy despite an explicit exclusion.
findings.trigger: For example, with proxy settings selected, request `https://[2001:db8::1]` and `NO_PROXY=[2001:db8::1]` (or `[2001:db8::1]:443`). The parser removes the closing bracket even when no `]:` port delimiter was present; the resulting entry does not match the host.

evidence.observation: The bracketed-entry branch splits on `]:` and unconditionally trims a trailing `]`; comparison then uses the still-bracketed host and its bracket-stripped form.

findings.verification: Add a unit test calling `proxy_decision("https", "[2001:db8::1]", None, Some(proxy), None, Some("[2001:db8::1]"))` and assert it returns false.
findings.remedy: Parse bracketed IPv6 entries without discarding the literal's closing bracket, and handle an optional port separately before comparing the normalized address.

history.evidence: proxy_decision_follows_scheme_and_no_proxy: NO_PROXY=[2001:db8::1] and [2001:db8::1]:443 exclude https://[2001:db8::1]; no_proxy_entry parses the bracketed literal and its port (commit after f811a0b)

findings.claim: NO_PROXY port qualifiers are discarded rather than matched against the request port, so exclusions apply to the host on the wrong ports.
findings.trigger: For `https://api.example:8443` with `NO_PROXY=api.example:443`, the helper strips `:443` and returns false (do not proxy), even though the port-qualified entry does not match the target port. The inverse mismatch also incorrectly bypasses the proxy.

evidence.observation: The helper removes a numeric port and has no target-port input. The existing test also expects `example.test:8080` to exclude a target without that port.

findings.verification: Add tests for matching and mismatching explicit target/NO_PROXY ports, including a target on 8443 with an entry on 443.
findings.remedy: Pass the parsed URL port into `proxy_decision` and require a port-qualified NO_PROXY entry to match that port; retain host-only matching for entries without a port.

history.evidence: proxy_decision takes the request port; NO_PROXY=api.example:443 no longer excludes port 8443 and example.test:8080 no longer excludes port 80 (unit test proxy_decision_follows_scheme_and_no_proxy)

findings.claim: The loopback guard misses IPv4-mapped IPv6 loopback literals, allowing them to be proxied.
findings.trigger: With a proxy selected, `proxy_decision("https", "[::ffff:127.0.0.1]", Some(proxy), None, None, None)` returns true; the same applies to the equivalent hexadecimal mapped address.

evidence.observation: The guard recognizes `127.*`, `localhost`, and exactly `[::1]`/`::1`, but does not parse IP literals or recognize IPv4-mapped IPv6 loopback.

findings.verification: Add a test asserting that `proxy_decision` returns false for `[::ffff:127.0.0.1]` and its canonical hexadecimal equivalent.
findings.remedy: Parse the host as an IP address and classify IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses by their embedded IPv4 address before selecting a proxy.

history.evidence: is_loopback_literal parses the host as an IpAddr; [::ffff:127.0.0.1] and [::ffff:7f00:1] are never proxied, [::ffff:8.8.8.8] still is (unit test)

findings.claim: A Unicode IDN spelling in C3_HTTP_AUTH_PROXY can fail to select proxy auth for the same endpoint, causing key mode instead.
findings.trigger: Set `C3_HTTP_AUTH_PROXY=bücher.example` and configure `base_url=https://bücher.example/v1`. URL parsing canonicalizes the endpoint hostname, but the list parser only lowercases its entry, so the host comparison can miss.

evidence.observation: The URL host and environment list are normalized by different code paths; the list path contains no IDNA canonicalization.

findings.verification: Add an auth-mode test using a Unicode IDN in both the base URL and C3_HTTP_AUTH_PROXY, and check that it selects the same mode as the equivalent punycode spelling.
findings.remedy: Canonicalize each auth-list hostname using the same IDNA/URL hostname rules as `HttpConfig::host()`, or reject noncanonical entries explicitly instead of silently falling back to key mode.

history.evidence: proxy_auth_hosts_from canonicalises each entry with url::Host::parse: bücher.example and XN--BCHER-KVA.example both match the parsed host xn--bcher-kva.example (unit test proxy_auth_host_list_is_parsed_and_matched_exactly_or_by_subdomain)

findings.claim: Proxy auth can suppress the key even when this adapter is not using an environment-selected proxy, so the advertised credential-attaching proxy may never see the request.
findings.trigger: Set `C3_HTTP_AUTH_PROXY=api.example.com` but leave `HTTPS_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY`, and their lowercase forms unset, or put the endpoint in NO_PROXY. The attempt selects proxy auth and sends no Authorization header while `proxy` is false.

evidence.observation: Auth selection and proxy selection are independent; no check requires an applicable proxy when proxy auth is selected.

findings.verification: Add an attempt-level test with the host listed for proxy auth and no applicable proxy, and verify whether the request is rejected or intentionally supported through documented transparent egress.
findings.remedy: If credential injection requires the ureq proxy, reject precheck when proxy auth is selected but `env_proxy_applies` is false; otherwise document and test the transparent-egress guarantee.

history.note: answered with a warning, not a refusal: an attempt in the proxy auth mode with no applicable proxy records 'proxy auth without a proxy ...' in its warnings (tests/http_engine.rs proxy_auth_host_sends_no_authorization_header_and_needs_no_key); a transparent egress proxy the environment does not name is a real deployment, so the request is not refused

reviewer_checks.note: The attempt now adds an explicit warning when proxy auth is selected but no environment proxy applies; the credentialless request remains intentionally allowed for transparent-proxy deployments.
The warning for proxy auth without a proxy was added.

findings.claim: An invalid numeric NO_PROXY port is treated as an unqualified host exclusion, which can disable the selected egress proxy for other ports.
findings.trigger: Set NO_PROXY=api.example:65536 and request https://api.example:8443. Parsing fails to produce a u16 port, returns the host with no port, and the later host match excludes the request.

evidence.observation: The port parse is converted to Option<u16>; None is subsequently treated as no port constraint, so the malformed port-qualified entry matches all ports.

findings.verification: Add a unit test asserting that an out-of-range port entry does not exclude a request on a different port.
findings.remedy: Reject or ignore an entry when it contains a port separator but the port is invalid; do not reinterpret it as a host-only entry.

history.evidence: 320f05e: no_proxy_entry returns None for example.test:65536, example.test:abc, [::1]:x; proxy_decision_follows_scheme_and_no_proxy asserts NO_PROXY=api.example:65536 no longer excludes port 8443

reviewer_checks.note: Invalid numeric NO_PROXY port still treated as host exclusion.

findings.claim: The proxy-auth allowlist accepts broad parent names such as a public suffix, allowing unrelated endpoints to enter header-less proxy-auth mode.
findings.trigger: Set C3_HTTP_AUTH_PROXY=com and configure a base URL such as https://attacker.example.com/v1. The suffix match selects HttpAuth::Proxy and the key-presence check is skipped.

evidence.observation: Entries are canonicalized as hosts but are not checked for public-suffix or single-label breadth; host matching intentionally includes every subdomain.

findings.verification: Add a test for a public-suffix entry and decide whether it must be refused or explicitly documented as a broad trust grant.
findings.remedy: Reject public-suffix and otherwise dangerously broad entries, or require exact-host matching unless subdomain trust is separately and explicitly enabled.

history.evidence: 320f05e: proxy_auth_hosts_from drops single-label entries (com, localhost); proxy_auth_host_list_is_parsed_and_matched_exactly_or_by_subdomain asserts attacker.example.com does not match a listing of com

reviewer_checks.note: Proxy-auth allowlist still accepts broad parent names.

findings.claim: A Linux PID reused within one second can compare as the same process even when the /proc-derived start timestamps differ.
findings.trigger: A stored process timestamp and a reused PID's timestamp differ by less than 1000 ms; the non-Windows comparator returns true.

evidence.observation: The Linux helper supplies a start timestamp, but same_start_time accepts any non-Windows difference strictly below one second.

findings.verification: Add a unit test with two distinct start timestamps separated by less than one second and verify that Linux liveness treats them as different.
findings.remedy: Compare Linux-generated timestamps exactly or within only the /proc clock-tick resolution; retain any broader tolerance only for platforms whose timestamps genuinely require it.

history.evidence: 320f05e: same_start_time tolerates 10 ms off Windows; start_times_match_within_one_tick_only asserts 5 ms same, 10 ms and 500 ms different

reviewer_checks.note: Linux PID reuse within one second can still cause false same-start-time match.

findings.claim: The non-Windows tree kill can silently miss descendants because descendants_of stops collecting after 4096 PIDs.
findings.trigger: A launched process tree has more than 4096 descendants; descendants beyond the cap are not returned, while kill_tree reports no survivors.

evidence.observation: The traversal condition stops adding and enqueuing once out.len() reaches 4096, and the caller kills only the returned list plus the child.

findings.verification: Add a traversal test with more than 4096 synthetic descendants and assert that truncation is either absent or explicitly reported.
findings.remedy: Do not silently cap the traversal; if a bound is required, return a truncation status and surface or handle the surviving PIDs.

history.evidence: 320f05e: descendants_in walks the whole table with a visited set; descendants_walk_the_whole_table_without_a_cap_or_a_loop asserts 5002 descendants, a self-parented row and no loop

reviewer_checks.note: Non-Windows tree kill still misses descendants beyond 4096 PIDs.

findings.claim: The IP-literal resolver change is shared and can affect Windows behavior; it is not confined to the Unix/Linux build.
findings.trigger: A Windows caller validates or uses an embedder URL with an IP literal in an environment where resolving that literal would fail or produce different results.

evidence.observation: host_addrs directly constructs SocketAddr values for IPv4 and IPv6 literals without a platform cfg, while domain names still use ToSocketAddrs.

findings.verification: Run the embedder URL tests on Windows, including IPv4 and IPv6 literals, and compare behavior against the base revision.
findings.remedy: If Windows behavior must remain unchanged, gate the direct-literal path to the intended platforms; otherwise document and test the cross-platform behavior change.

history.note: the direct construction of a SocketAddr from an IP literal gives the same address std's resolver returns for a literal (127.0.0.1 is parsed, never resolved) and the same ::1 the Windows resolver returned for [::1] (the base revision's test passed there); the Windows result for a valid literal is unchanged and the ubuntu/windows CI runs the same loopback tests on both

reviewer_checks.note: IP-literal resolver change is shared and affects Windows behavior.

findings.claim: An invalid numeric NO_PROXY port is treated as an unqualified host exclusion, which can disable the selected egress proxy for other ports.
findings.trigger: Setting NO_PROXY to a value containing a host with an invalid port number (e.g., 'example.com:99999').

evidence.observation: The function no_proxy_entry returns (host, None) when the port string is not a valid u16, causing the host to be matched without port consideration in proxy_decision.

findings.verification: Set NO_PROXY=example.com:99999 and verify that a request to example.com:80 (or any other port) bypasses the proxy even if a proxy is configured for that port.
findings.remedy: Treat an invalid port as making the entire NO_PROXY entry invalid (ignore it) or require a valid port for the entry to be considered.

history.note: the same finding as F09-1 (the free reviewer restated the open findings of handoff 09); tracked there

findings.claim: The proxy-auth allowlist accepts broad parent names such as a public suffix, allowing unrelated endpoints to enter header-less proxy-auth mode.
findings.trigger: Setting C3_HTTP_AUTH_PROXY to a public suffix (e.g., 'co.uk').

evidence.observation: The function host_uses_proxy_auth returns true for any host that ends with the suffix (e.g., 'example.co.uk' matches suffix 'co.uk').

findings.verification: Set C3_HTTP_AUTH_PROXY=co.uk and verify that a request to http://example.co.uk/ uses the proxy auth mode (no Authorization header sent) even though the proxy was not intended for this host.
findings.remedy: Use a proper domain matching library that requires a dot boundary and does not match public suffixes (e.g., match only if the host is exactly the suffix or has a dot boundary before the suffix).

history.note: the same finding as F09-2 (the free reviewer restated the open findings of handoff 09); tracked there

findings.claim: A Linux PID reused within one second can compare as the same process even when the /proc-derived start timestamps differ.
findings.trigger: A PID is reused within one second (e.g., process A exits at time T, process B starts at time T+0.5s with the same PID).

evidence.observation: The function same_start_time returns true if the absolute difference in start times is less than 1000 milliseconds, allowing a reused PID within one second to be considered the same process.

findings.verification: Create two processes with the same PID within one second and verify that pid_alive considers the second process as still alive when using the first process's start time.
findings.remedy: Reduce the tolerance to zero (exact match) or use a higher-resolution start time source if available, noting that the /proc start time has 10ms resolution.

history.note: the same finding as F09-3 (the free reviewer restated the open findings of handoff 09); tracked there

findings.claim: The non-Windows tree kill can silently miss descendants because descendants_of stops collecting after 4096 PIDs.
findings.trigger: A process tree with more than 4096 descendants.

evidence.observation: The function descendants_of limits the output list to 4096 PIDs, causing excess descendants to be omitted from the kill list.

findings.verification: Create a process tree with over 4096 descendants and verify that some descendants are not killed by the non-Windows tree kill.
findings.remedy: Remove the limit or increase it to a safe number (e.g., the maximum number of processes on the system), or change the algorithm to kill as it walks the tree without storing all PIDs.

history.note: the same finding as F09-4 (the free reviewer restated the open findings of handoff 09); tracked there
